name: io.github.RectaBuild/recta
title: Recta
description: Proven cheaper USDC bridge route for AI agents (Across, CCTP, Stargate); fee 5% of verified saving

tools.name: recta_preflight
tools.description: Call before any cross-chain USDC/USDT transfer. Give the corridor and the amount (and, optionally, baseline_provider: the route you would use; without it Recta compares against lifi, LI.FI's own quote, or across where LI.FI does not apply). Returns, for your route, its estimated total cost in USDC and when it arrives; and, when Recta proves a cheaper route, the saving (a proven lower bound), Recta's 5 % fee, that route's total cost and arrival (the route itself is not named) and execute_via_recta: sign the same request to get the route. No wallet and no address needed (sender, recipient, constraints and gas ceilings are filled when absent and listed in `assumed`; your own sender gives the most exact figure). Stores nothing, charges nothing; 3 a day per IP address.

source_network.description: Lowercase network as in the service descriptor, e.g. base, ethereum, arbitrum.

amount.description: How much of source_asset to send, in whole tokens (not cents, not wei): "100" with USDC means 100 USDC. Minimum 3.5 for stablecoins (about 3.5 USD). No maximum.

baseline_provider.description: Optional: the route you would use without Recta, e.g. lifi, across, stargate_v2, cctp_v2_standard (recta_fit_check lists the ones a corridor admits). Absent: lifi, or across where LI.FI does not apply.

sender.description: Optional: your own sending address, for the most exact figure.

body.description: Alternative to the fields above: the whole evaluation request body (from recta_request_template), as a JSON object.

tools.name: recta_about
tools.description: Start here for the full guide; to check a transfer, call recta_preflight. Call Recta before your agent moves stablecoins from one blockchain to another (a bridge or cross-chain transfer): give it the route you would use anyway, and it answers, for free, whether a cheaper route exists at the same chain state and proves the saving. If there is none, nothing is charged. Transfers start on: arbitrum, arc, avalanche, base, bnb_chain, ethereum, hyperevm, ink, linea, monad, optimism, polygon, unichain. They can arrive on: arbitrum, arc, avalanche, base, bnb_chain, ethereum, hyperevm, ink, linea, monad, optimism, polygon, robinhood_chain, solana_mainnet, tron_mainnet, unichain. Assets: USDC, USDC_BINANCE_PEG, USDG, USDT, USDT_BINANCE_PEG, USDT_OP_BRIDGED. Amounts: at least 3.5 tokens of a stablecoin (about 3.5 USD), no maximum. The exact corridors are in the service descriptor. Returns the full guide (llms.txt): what Recta is, the fee (5 % of the verified saving, nothing if none) and the call flow.

tools.name: recta_status
tools.description: Call before relying on Recta in a run: whether it is ready to evaluate now, and its contract version.

tools.name: recta_service_descriptor
tools.description: Call to check whether a planned cross-chain transfer is covered: the supported corridors (source and destination networks and assets), the bridges compared (Across, CCTP, Stargate, USDT0 and others), amount ranges, limits and the JSON Schema of every request and response.

tools.name: recta_fit_check
tools.description: Call first, before a cross-chain stablecoin transfer: whether Recta covers the corridor, which routes it compares, which route you can declare as yours, and the contracts a route would touch. Unsigned, free, never reveals a route or a saving.

source_network.description: Lowercase network as in the service descriptor, e.g. base, ethereum, arbitrum.

tools.name: recta_saving_odds
tools.description: How many recorded decisions on this corridor found a saving, by amount range (counts and dates only, never per route). Unsigned and free; use it to decide whether a signed evaluation is worth it.

source_network.description: Lowercase network as in the service descriptor, e.g. base, ethereum, arbitrum.

baseline_provider.description: Accepted and ignored: the odds are for the whole corridor.

tools.name: recta_request_template
tools.description: Returns the full body of the evaluation request for a corridor, an amount and the route you would use anyway (baseline_provider): you fill only your sender, recipient and gas ceilings, then sign it with recta_prepare_signed_request and recta_send_signed_request.

source_network.description: Lowercase network as in the service descriptor, e.g. base, ethereum, arbitrum.

amount.description: How much of source_asset to send, in whole tokens (not cents, not wei): "100" with USDC means 100 USDC. Minimum 3.5 for stablecoins (about 3.5 USD). No maximum.

baseline_provider.description: The route you would use without Recta (see recta_fit_check's declarable_baselines).

tools.name: recta_trial_evaluation
tools.description: Unsigned trial of an evaluation: send the evaluation request body (from recta_request_template; no wallet and no address needed: without sender and recipient Recta reads a stand-in address, listed in `assumed`; any sender other than the zero address and any recipient of the destination network's kind are read as given) and get whether a cheaper provable route exists for this exact transfer, the saving (lower bound, USDC) and Recta's 5 % of it. Names no route, stores nothing, charges nothing; 3 a day per IP address. To get the route, sign the same body with recta_prepare_signed_request and recta_send_signed_request.

body.description: The evaluation request body, as a JSON object or its JSON text.

tools.name: recta_prepare_signed_request
tools.description: Step 1 of a free quote for a cross-chain transfer. Computes the exact message the agent's EVM wallet must sign (EIP-191 personal_sign) for one Recta request, and the headers to send. Holds no key and calls nothing. Then call recta_send_signed_request with the same method, path, idempotency_key, body and issued_at, plus the signature. Start with POST /v1/golden-corridor/commercial-evaluations (body: recta_request_template; its "sender" must be the signing address). If you have no wallet tool that can personal_sign, this server cannot sign for you: No signing code needed: the npm package @recta/client builds, checks and signs the request for you, and @recta/mcp (`npx -y @recta/mcp`) is a local MCP server that does it as tools: without a key it offers only the free fit check and trial; with RECTA_PRIVATE_KEY of a dedicated wallet (kept on your machine) it signs too. Evaluations are free and need no funds. Paying a fee needs the fee in USDC on Base and a USDC allowance to Permit2 (an ERC-20 approve of USDC to Permit2). If the transfer itself starts from USDC on Base, the wallet needs the transfer amount plus the fee.

body.description: The exact JSON body text, byte for byte as it will be sent. Empty for GET.

tools.name: recta_send_signed_request
tools.description: Step 2: sends the request signed by the agent's own wallet to a Recta route and returns its HTTP status and JSON body. POST /v1/golden-corridor/commercial-evaluations returns, free, a decision (whether a cheaper route than the one the agent would use anyway is proven, and the saving) or an abstention; GET /v1/golden-corridor/commercial-evaluations/{result_id}/execution-artifact then asks for the fee ceiling's signature and, once it is signed, returns the route's transactions. Executing a decision's route creates a fee of 5 % of the verified saving, capped by the permit the agent signs; no saving, no fee.
